> **Status (v0.4, task 4.7): the Parakeet engine is the default on corpus A. N2 for Parakeet is not confirmed yet: the v0.4 acceptance measures `total` from ≥ 20 PTT dictations (15, v0.4 acceptance).**
> - Run `2026-10-07T22-56-03Z` on **corpus A** (40 utterances), 3 repetitions. Conditions: AC, `performance` platform profile, external cooling on, browsers closed, VS Code open, daemon stopped. The package was at 57 °C and the load average at 0.18 at the start.
> - The matrix has the two engines of v0.4 only: Parakeet with 4 and 8 threads, and `small-q8_0` with 4 and 8 threads at `audio_ctx = 1000`. Beam search and `whisper-bench` were not run. The full Whisper matrix is in the 2026-10-03 section below.
> - `small-q8_0` t=4 at the full window was added after the main run, in the same run directory (`--resume`). The audio_ctx rule of 13 §13.5 needs it. That run started after 3 min of cooling (53 °C). `system.json` does not list it.
> - **Default: Parakeet, 4 threads** — WER 5.6 %, p90 text_ready **0.93 s**, peak RSS 1585 MB. Against `small-q8_0` t=4 ctx=1000 on the same day, WER is 1.8 pp lower and p90 is 3× shorter (2.80 s). It also meets the v0.4 WER threshold (≤ 7.4 %).
> - **Short utterances improve most:** WER on the `short` group is 10.9 % for Parakeet and 18.1 % for `small-q8_0` @1000. The `difficult` group is 14.8 % and 18.0 %.
> - **8 threads do not help Parakeet.** p90 increases from 0.93 to 1.23 s, and peak RSS increases to 2188 MB, which is more than N1 (1.6 GB). For `small-q8_0`, 8 threads decrease p90 by 6 % only (2.80 → 2.64 s). The report excludes `small-q8_0` t=8 @1000 because there is no t=8 full-window run, not because of its results.
> - **The RAM margin is small.** The Parakeet peak RSS is 1585 MB, and the N1 limit is 1638 MB (1.6 × 1024, the unit of `peak RSS MB`). That is a margin of 3 %. Task 4.1 measured a peak of 1.55 GB. The peak increases with the recording length: a fresh server reached 1563 MB at 60 s and 2096 MB at 120 s. After the medium group, 60 s and 120 s in one process, the peak was 2529–2540 MB, which is more than `MemoryMax=2500M`. PTT allows 120 s (`ptt.max_duration_s`), so task 4.8 examines this. Scripts and results: `~/.local/share/local-stt/bench/rss-2026-10-08/`.
> - **Whisper is faster than on 2026-10-03, with the same WER.** `small-q8_0` @1000 p90 is 2.80 s (3.67 s on 2026-10-03), and at the full window it is 4.26 s (5.57 s). The full window now meets the 5 s rule too. The cause is probably the external cooling and the idle machine. This is not a code change: the transcripts and WER are the same.
> - Thermals: the CPU still reached 99–100 °C during the Parakeet t=4 configuration, and 87–98 °C in the others. The lowest frequency was 1775–2700 MHz (1337 MHz on 2026-10-03).
> - Found during this task: `bench report` used the whisper-server N1 limit (1 GB) for every engine, so it excluded Parakeet. The report now uses the N1 limit of each engine (13 §13.5) and names `stt.engine` in the default.

**Provisional default:** `stt.engine = "parakeet"`, `stt.threads = 4`. N2 remains unconfirmed until the v0.1 measurement of `total`.

Excluded configurations:

- `parakeet-tdt-0.6b-v3-int8|t8|ctx0|bs-1`: peak server RSS 2188 MB > 1.6 GB (N1)
- `small-q8_0|t8|ctx1000|bs-1`: audio_ctx costs > 1.0 pp WER vs the full window (or no audio_ctx=0 run)

> **Status: default selected on corpus A; N2 confirmed in the v0.1 acceptance (2026-10-04): p90 `total` 3.70 s over 20 dictations of 4–10 s with injection into five applications ([acceptance-v0.1.md](acceptance-v0.1.md#n2-ptt-latency)).**
> - Run `2026-10-03T09-10-49Z` on **corpus A** (13.2A, the user's own voice, microphone and room; 40 utterances), same matrix as the 2026-09-17 corpus-B run. Conditions: AC, `performance` platform profile, VS Code open, package 74 °C at start, 82–86 °C for most of the run (99 °C only during the first configuration).
> - Default: `small-q8_0`, `threads = 4`, `audio_ctx = 1000` — WER 7.4 %, p90 text_ready 3.73 → **3.67 s**, peak RSS 467 MB. It is again the only production configuration with p90 ≤ 5 s, so the corpus-B selection (2026-09-17) stands. N2 is confirmed only by the v0.1 `total` measurement with injection (13 §13.5).
> - WER on corpus A is about a third of corpus B (7.4 % vs 24.1 % for the default); latency is within 2 % of the corpus-B run.
> - `audio_ctx = 1000` costs nothing on the whole corpus for `small-q8_0` (7.5 → 7.4 %) and saves ~35 % latency; for `small-q5_1` it costs 0.9 pp (7.8 → 8.7 %). Both stay inside the 1 pp limit of 13 §13.5.
> - Runner-up `small-q5_1` @1000 is worse here (8.7 %) and again just above N2 (p90 5.07 s); beam 5 gains 0.5–1.1 pp but costs 1.2–1.5 s p90.
> - **Short utterances are the weak spot:** `small-q8_0` @1000 has 18.1 % WER on the `short` group (12 sentences of 3–5 words, so one wrong word ≈ 2 pp) vs 7.1 % on `medium`. This is the typical PTT case — revisit in v0.1/v0.2 (VAD trimming, prompt).
> - `difficult` (4 sentences only): `audio_ctx = 1000` scores 18.0 % vs 14.8 % with the full window — a signal, not a conclusion, at this sample size.
> - `medium-q5_0` halves the error (3.8 % vs 7.6 % on the medium group) but needs p50 15.0 s even @1000 — eliminated on this CPU.
> - Not measured on corpus A: `small` (f16), 8 threads, the `long/` continuous recording (soak test, v0.2), `total` with injection (v0.1).

## Stage 3 — soak test, continuous mode (2026-10-04, task 2.9)

`local-stt bench --soak --words ~/stt-corpus/long/001.whisper-large-v3-turbo.json` with the production default `small-q8_0`, 4 threads, `audio_ctx = 1000`: corpus A `long/001.wav` (497 s, the user reading `long_pl.txt`) looped for 10 min through the daemon's own chain (13 §13.4). Raw results: `~/.local/share/local-stt/bench/soak-2026-10-04/`.

**No battery on the reference machine** (user decision 2026-10-04): the battery run of 13 §13.5 is replaced by the `power-saver` platform profile on AC (firmware profile `quiet`).

| Run | Conditions | RTF (≤ 0.5) | queue max | queue slope, final 5 min (≤ 0.05 s/min) | freq drop (≤ 30 %) | temp max | VAD, N4 (≤ 5 %) | Verdict |
|---|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---|
| 1 | `performance`, after another load; browsers and two VS Code windows open | 0.56 | 17.2 s | +0.108 | 15 % | 100 °C | 2.1 % | FAIL (RTF, slope) |
| 2 | `power-saver` (`quiet`), 5 min after run 1 | 1.99 | 64.2 s | — | — | 59 °C | 5.6 % | FAIL: backlog stop after 3.5 min |
| 3 | `performance`, cooled to 44 °C, browsers closed (load average 0.58, VS Code 6 % CPU) | **0.33** | 14.6 s | −0.115 | 27 % | 99 °C | 1.6 % | **PASS** |

- **Continuous mode with `small-q8_0` passes on an unloaded machine** (run 3): no separate `stt.continuous_model` is needed. The margin is thin on CPU frequency (27 % sustained drop against the 30 % limit at 99 °C), and run 1 shows that background load (browsers, editors) is enough to fail it.
- **`power-saver` does not sustain continuous mode** with this model: RTF ≈ 2, the queue reached `continuous.max_backlog_s` (60 s) and the daemon stopped dictation as designed (04 §4.3, *Backlog*). Its VAD share (5.6 %) also exceeds N4; the RMS pre-filter of 05 §5.4 is not implemented, since N4 holds on `performance`.
- Segmentation was identical in runs 1 and 3 (74 segments: 63 `silence`, 10 `max_length` = 13.5 %, 1 `flush` at the stop), as expected from the deterministic Segmenter.
- **Incorrect cuts: not measured meaningfully.** The automatic reference (whisper-cli `large-v3-turbo-q5_0`, token timestamps combined into words) puts no gap between 459 of 765 adjacent words and stretches words over pauses (e.g. “badanie” 1.66 s), so cuts in pauses count as inside a word; the reported 33/73 is an artefact. A manually verified `long/001.words.json` (13 §13.3) is still needed for this metric.

## History — interim public corpus B (2026-09-17)

Run `2026-09-17T16-28-19Z` on `~/stt-corpus-public` (13.2B: FLEURS + Wolne Lektury audiobook, other speakers, studio-like audio, no `short` group). It produced the provisional default that corpus A later confirmed. Notes from that run:

> - Run on the interim public corpus (13.2B), not corpus A. Rerun on corpus A before fixing the defaults for good.
> - Provisional default: `small-q8_0`, `threads = 4`, `audio_ctx = 1000` (WER 24.1 %, p90 text_ready 3.73 s, peak RSS 442 MB). Approved by the user on 2026-09-17 under the 13 §13.5 rule with N2 = 5 s.
> - Runner-up `small-q5_1` @1000 is 1.8 pp better (WER 22.3 %) but measured p90 5.07 s and 5.10 s in two runs, i.e. above N2 before injection is even counted; the user chose the configuration that satisfies the rule.
> - Repeatability check (run `2026-09-17T18-48-42Z-rerun-ctx1000`, both `@1000` configurations, whole corpus): p50/p90 within 0.6–4.7 % of this run and all 84 transcripts per configuration identical character for character. On a cool, idle machine on AC the spread is far below the ±20 % seen in the first session.
> - `audio_ctx = 1000` costs at most 0.8 pp WER (`small-q8_0` 23.3 → 24.1 %) and saves 30–37 % latency; for `small-q5_1` it slightly improved WER (22.7 → 22.3 %). Both stay inside the 1 pp limit of 13 §13.5.
> - Request history matters (06 §6.7): `small-q8_0` @1000 scores 23.8 % WER on the medium group alone (stage 1) and 24.2 % when the same files are interleaved with longer full-window recordings (stage 2). Stage 2 is the production-like order.
> - `medium-q5_0` is eliminated even with `audio_ctx = 1000` (p50 15.1 s), and `large-v3-turbo-q5_0` is far slower still (whisper-bench encoder 39.3 s vs 20.6 s for medium).
> - `small` (f16), measured separately on 2026-09-18 (run `2026-09-18T18-53-52Z-small-f16`, same runner and order): @1000 WER 23.7 %, p90 4.56 s, peak RSS 658 MB; full window WER 22.7 %, p90 6.67 s. @1000 meets N2 but is within 1 pp of the default (−0.4 pp), so the 13 §13.5 tie-break (lower peak RAM) keeps `small-q8_0` (442 MB) as the default. Cross-run comparison: WER is deterministic, latency on this machine repeats within a few %.
> - Not measured here: 8 threads (≤ 3 % gain in the first run), the `short` group (missing from the public corpus), and `total` with injection (v0.1, 13 §13.5).
